headline: Digestion breaks down food into absorbable molecules—complex inputs become simple, usable components
universal_truth: Complexity must be simplified before it can be used; breaking things down is often the first step
fun_facts: Your digestive tract is about 30 feet long—a processing plant coiled inside you
Digestion starts in your mouth: saliva contains enzymes that begin breaking down starches
Your stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve metal—your stomach lining replaces itself every few days to survive it
discussion_questions: What complex inputs do you need to 'digest' before using?
How do you break down overwhelming information?
What's your process for making the complex simple?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You eat a sandwich—bread, meat, lettuce—but your cells can't use sandwiches. Digestion disassembles food into fundamental molecules: amino acids, sugars, fatty acids. Only then can cells absorb and use them. Breakdown precedes absorption.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often want to use things directly, but complex inputs require processing. What does digestion teach us about handling complexity?

options.text: Complex inputs must be simplified before they can be absorbed and used—breaking down into components is the first step of integration
options.response: Yes. Your cells can't absorb a steak—only amino acids. Complexity must be reduced before use. This applies to information, projects, and problems too.
Smaller, yes, but also chemically simpler—proteins become amino acids, starches become sugars...

q1.title: Sequential Processing
q1.script: Digestion happens in stages: mouth, stomach, intestines—each with specific tasks. Complex processing often requires sequential steps, each building on the last.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Sequential Processing"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Enzymes as Tools
q2.script: Enzymes are specialized molecular tools—each breaks specific bonds. Amylase breaks starches. Protease breaks proteins. The right tools for the right substrates. Specialization enables efficiency.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Mental Digestion
q3.script: Information requires digestion too. Complex ideas must be broken into understandable pieces. Reading isn't understanding—digesting is. Process before claiming comprehension.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Complexity must be simplified before it can be used. Breaking things down is often the first step. Digest before absorbing.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 244—welcome to September! Tomorrow, we'll explore getting rid of waste. Until then, notice how you break down complex inputs.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Digestion Practice - Break It Down
growTrack.learning_objective: Apply breakdown thinking to complex inputs
growTrack.activity: Take something complex you're trying to learn or use—a book, a skill, a project. Break it into digestible pieces. What are the fundamental components? Digest before trying to absorb. Simplify before integrating.
